utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I meant 1990, and in the other answer, I said from the 19th of August until the 2nd of September, whereas I see here a different date, the 17th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: The plebiscite was held and what was the turnout like and what were the views stated by the population?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The turnout was, if I can put it in descriptive terms, almost 100 per cent. That is to say that a large percentage of people voted. The plebiscite or rather this expression of views was held in the territory of Croatia throughout Yugoslavia and abroad. That is to say that Serbs from Croatia who did not even live in Croatia at that time voted, and then there were interpretations in terms of whether there was even a turnout greater than 100 per cent. A large number of Serbs turned out, and 99 per cent or whatever of those who voted in the referendum voted in favour of autonomy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: So the Serb people in Croatia who took part in this referendum, did they state their views on their autonomy in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In December 1990, did the Serb National Council and the temporary Presidency of the municipalities of Dalmatia and Lika proclaim the Serb Autonomous Region of Krajina and did they adopt the Statute of the Krajina?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: This Serb Autonomous Region of Krajina, according to this statute and according to the decision establishing it, is it defined as a form of territorial autonomy within the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can it be said that the Serbian National Council, as a temporary executive organ of the Serb assembly and of the Serbs, observing the results of the plebiscite, reached a decision on the establishment of a Serb autonomous region, the Serb Autonomous Region of Krajina as an integral part of the Republic of Croatia an autonomy within Croatia, so did they respect the political will of the Serb people?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serb National Council only proclaimed the decisions that were reached by the assemblies of the municipalities that constituted the municipalities of western -- of Northern Dalmatia and Lika. So it was renamed into the Serb Autonomous Region of Krajina. So it's not that the Serb National Council reached the decision, they only proclaimed that the municipalities confirmed the status and that the Serb Autonomous Region of Krajina was established as an integral part of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: That's right, Mr. Babic. Thank you for your answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that it is time for the adjournment now. It is quarter to 2. We shall continue when the Trial Chamber tells us that we will.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I -- just a small matter. It's happened a couple of times. It's a minor point but nonetheless I raise it. I would just ask if the Court could ask Defence counsel to refrain from saying to the witness, "That's right," when he's given answers, after he's given certain answers, he says, "that's right, Mr. Babic." It seems to me that's a subjective argument.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Apart from it being the subject of argument are, it's a kind of unacceptable echo in the recording of the proceedings, Mr. Milovancevic. It's just something that is discouraged in these fora. I don't know how you take that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I accept what you've said to me with full respect, with a brief explanation. The witness corrected me. My question was not fully in line with what he had been saying so then I confirmed that he said what he said, not wishing to influence the witness in any way. Of course, I shall bear in mine the instructions of the Trial Chamber. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Milovancevic. The matter stands adjourned to the 2nd of March at quarter past 2 in Courtroom I, this courtroom. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 2nd day of March, 2006, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.49 p.m.,
